- Prepared head SHA: [03668591e16da65e5c9512c14e3c13a9fed677bb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128131/commits/03668591e16da65e5c9512c14e3c13a9fed677bb)

Heads-up on a billing consequence of this change that I don't think was intended, confirmed with Anthropic support today.

## What changed

Before this PR, the backend spawned Claude Code in print mode — `CLAUDE_CLI_DEFAULT_ARGS` leads with `-p`. Claude Code reports that invocation as entrypoint **`sdk-cli`**.

After it, `agent-sdk.runtime.ts` strips `-p` / `--print` via `CLAUDE_STREAM_PROTOCOL_FLAGS` and hands off to the Agent SDK's `query()`, which stamps `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT="sdk-ts"` whenever the variable is unset. Core clears any inherited value (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` is in `CLAUDE_CLI_CLEAR_ENV`) and never re-injects it, so it is always unset and the child is always **`sdk-ts`**.

## Why that matters

Anthropic meters those two entrypoints against different pools. Per support, since 2026-06-15 Agent SDK usage no longer counts toward a Claude subscription's usage limits; Max 20x instead gets a separate **$200/month Agent SDK credit**. When that credit is exhausted, requests fall through to usage credits, and if those aren't enabled the request fails with:

```
API Error: 400 You're out of extra usage. Add more at claude.ai/settings/usage and keep going.
```

So this PR silently moved every Claude-subscription OpenClaw user from plan-metered usage onto a finite monthly credit.

## Evidence from one affected machine

Claude Code transcripts record the entrypoint per turn. On this host, `sdk-ts` appears for the first time on 2026-08-24 — the day this landed — and the billing errors begin the same day. Volume for a single day once the credit ran out:

| entrypoint | turns | cache-creation tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk-ts` (Agent SDK credit) | 152 | 3,932,195 |
| `sdk-cli` (plan) | 185 | 2,777,612 |
| `claude-desktop` (plan) | 1,316 | 5,893,604 |

Interactive `claude -p` on the same account and machine keeps working throughout, including at high context and with `--effort max`. Only `sdk-ts` turns fail. Failed turns record `duration_api_ms: 0`, `total_cost_usd: 0` and zero tokens — rejected pre-flight, so they don't appear as usage anywhere obvious.

## Why this is worth addressing

The failure text says the account is out of usage, which sends operators to check their plan, their credentials, and their config — none of which are wrong. On this machine it cost most of a day to trace, and it looks identical to an auth problem: `models auth list` shows no Anthropic profile (correct after #129052), the native login is healthy, and every model fails on a six-character prompt.

Suggestions, in rough priority:

1. **Say so somewhere.** A changelog note and/or a `doctor` check would have collapsed this to a minute. Right now nothing in OpenClaw indicates which billing path a run takes.
